sources.entry: Phosphene - Use any video as your macOS wallpaper on the desktop and the lock screen, picked directly from System Settings. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/kageroumado/phosphene) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Phosphene
summary.one_liner: Phosphene is a free, open-source macOS app that lets you use your own videos as desktop and lock screen wallpapers, selected in System Settings.
use_cases: Set a personal video as a macOS desktop background
Show a looping video on the macOS lock screen
Convert Wallpaper Engine Steam Workshop wallpapers for use on a Mac
Use different video wallpapers on each display or Space
Replace static wallpapers with animated ones without extra CPU drain on battery
summary.what_it_does: Phosphene plays user-supplied videos as wallpapers on the macOS desktop and lock screen by using Apple's wallpaper framework, so macOS runs the wallpaper alongside its built-in collections. Videos are added by dragging them into the library or menu bar, then selected in System Settings → Wallpaper. It supports MP4, MOV, HEVC, H.264, and ProRes files that the Mac can decode, and can set wallpapers per display and per Space with frame-accurate, gapless looping. It pauses on battery, dimming, occlusion, and thermal limits, and stops processing after 30 seconds idle. It can also convert Wallpaper Engine wallpapers from the Steam Workshop into looping video wallpapers.
notable: Uses Apple's wallpaper framework so macOS itself plays the videos, selectable in System Settings
Converts Wallpaper Engine Steam Workshop wallpapers into video wallpapers
Pauses on battery, dimming, occlusion, and thermal limits to save power
Free and open source under the MIT license
caveats: Wallpaper Engine wallpapers come from a Windows program; Phosphene needs Steam Workshop subscriptions, and the page says Wallpaper Engine runs in Windows Steam, with Sevoflurane offered to bring Steam to a Mac (a separate developer's product)
